gk02538_direct_controls.catalog_layout: 四周雙邊; 半葉匡郭 25.3×17.5cm; 9行21字; 注雙行; 上下花紋魚尾; 34.7×22.5cm

direct_visual_adjudication.safe_reading: The dated calendar images are valid institutional/type-family controls, but their annual-calendar imposition, mixed type sizes and chained calendar formulae are not a copy-identical layout standard for the 12-juan Datonglizhu commentary. Layout comparison cannot close GK02538's impression date.

indexed_abstract_adjudication: The study warns that different printing types were often lumped under one Kwansanggam Type label and that catalogues can therefore contain erroneous type notes.
It proposes four distinct functional type categories: Daetongryokja, Naeyongsamsoja, Myongsiryokja, and Chiljongryokja.

ryu_series_bibliographic_control.common_layout: 四周單邊; 行字數不定; 註雙行; 黑口; 上下內向三葉花紋魚尾

chronology_adjudication.next_required_evidence: shared-glyph/type-body/form comparison or specialist bibliographic identification that explicitly binds GK02538 to a dated Gwansanggam subtype/generation

unresolved_lineage_questions: Which one of the specialist Gwansanggam type subtypes, if any, can be securely assigned to GK02538?
Can a set of shared glyphs between GK02538 and dated pre/post-Imjin calendar controls identify a casting generation or merely a broad calligraphic family?
Which securely pre-1578 witness carries the exact Sanming/Yueling Rainwater 後四日 + Dahan 十三後日 fingerprint?
transmission_impact.interpretation: 12EH creates a direct dated physical comparison corpus and narrows the chronology method. It does not date GK02538; instead it rejects page-layout shortcutting and requires subtype/shared-glyph evidence.

next_gate: Acquire or derive shared-glyph crop controls between GK02538 and dated Inryeokja objects, preserving scale/source metadata.
Seek the 1987 specialist study/full bibliographic evidence or another authoritative type study that can classify GK02538 to a specific Gwansanggam subtype.
Continue exact pre-1578 Sanming/Yueling combined fingerprint and threshold-operator searches.
